newsitem.title: LEBANON: Beirut bank shares shine, rally seen continuing.
newsitem.headline: Beirut bank shares shine, rally seen continuing.

text.p: Bank shares continued to rise on the Beirut Stock Exchange in the week ended on Friday and dealers said they expected them to continue rallying next week.
Solidere, Lebanon's biggest company, was mixed and the other four listed companies were inactive.
The BLOM stock index fell 0.35 percent to 908.54 while the LISPI share index rose 0.22 percent to 81.58.
Banque Audi's month-long rise slowed slightly, reaching $17.25 from last week's $17.00, an increase of 1.47 percent. Turnover rose to 162,310 shares from 153,195.

Banque Libanaise pour le Commerce rose two percent to $12.5 from $12.25. BLC, the first bank to list on the exchange, reached $12.625 on Tuesday but then fell back. BLC turnover jumped to 102,706 from 35,500.
BLC announced on Friday a 194 percent increase in 1996 pre-tax profits to $9.54 million from $3.25 million.
Dealers said they expected bank shares, in particular Audi, to continue to perform strongly.
"I see no reason why Audi should not continue to rise," a dealer told Reuters.
"As long as Audi holds up, I think BLC will hold up also. People see that the banking sector is a profitable sector," he said.
The expected listing of two more banks soon would boost trading further on the Beirut Stock Exchange, he added.
"People are hungry for instruments. Once Byblos Bank and Bank of Beirut join the market it should become more interesting."
Market turnover rose to 527,247 from 376,559 during the week and value rose to $6,602,540 from $4,684,173.
Solidere A shares, distributed to former holders of property rights in the Beirut central district Solidere is rebuilding, fell to $10.5 from $10.625.
B shares, issued in a $650-million subscription in January 1994, were unchanged at $10.875.
"There is nothing new on the Solidere front. The shares have not changed their price in the last three or four days," a dealer said.
There was no trade in the four other listed firms: Uniceramic, Eternit, Ciments Libanais and Ciments Blancs.
